title: Checking a Different Event Report

source.rights: 原创 AI 辅助虚构教学材料；尚待独立教学与发音审核。

questions.evidence: Nora: Our representative said that the event was planned for Sunday from one until five. The earlier note said noon, so the editor asked for confirmation before the press received the new schedule.
questions.explanation: 对话的新安排是周日下午一点到五点；中午是旧通知，周六属于阅读。

questions.prompt: Why did the editor ask for confirmation?
options: The historian refused to discuss the map.
An earlier note gave a different time.
answers: An earlier note gave a different time.
questions.evidence: Nora: Our representative said that the event was planned for Sunday from one until five. The earlier note said noon, so the editor asked for confirmation before the press received the new schedule.
questions.explanation: 旧通知写中午，与新时间不同，所以编辑要求确认。

questions.prompt: Where will the map be displayed?
options: At the back of the conference room.

questions.prompt: How old is the neighborhood view on the map?
questions.evidence:

Nora: Yes. She said that it showed the neighborhood twenty years ago. The transcript contains her exact words, and she agreed that the reporter could check the date with her.
questions.explanation: 历史学家说地图展示二十年前；五十年是阅读中不同地图的数字。

questions.prompt: What does the volunteer want before agreeing to be quoted?
options: To decide the opening time alone.
To review the full article before publication.

instructions: This dialogue is fictional. Audio is pending; once recorded, listen before reading the transcript.
transcript:
Nora: The reporter from the community newspaper called about our exhibition. She wants a short description before she writes her article.
Pavel: What did we tell her about the time?
Nora: Our representative said that the event was planned for Sunday from one until five. The earlier note said noon, so the editor asked for confirmation before the press received the new schedule.
Pavel: Good. The change is not a promise that every visitor can enter at once. We should explain that the room has limited space.
Nora: The journalist also asked where the historical map would be displayed. I told her it would be beside the entrance, not near the window.
Pavel: Did the historian offer an explanation of the map?
Nora: Yes. She said that it showed the neighborhood twenty years ago. The transcript contains her exact words, and she agreed that the reporter could check the date with her.
Pavel: One witness described last month's planning meeting. Her viewpoint is useful for that meeting, but she cannot describe the building from a century ago.
Nora: Another volunteer gave a speech about local heritage. She said that she might accept an offer to be quoted, but she wanted to see the sentence first. She could also decline.
Pavel: Did anyone deny that the map is a copy?
Nora: No. The statement makes clear that it is a copy. The editor plans to edit the article so readers do not confuse it with an original object.
Pavel: Please inform the photographer that we still need the volunteer's answer about the picture. We should warn the team not to assume permission.
Nora: I will ask her to respond this afternoon. A different visitor offered another perspective on the market, so the journalist may include both views without claiming that everyone agrees.
Pavel: That sounds useful. At the conference tomorrow, we can tell the group which details are confirmed and which still need checking.
Nora: I will bring the revised note and the transcript. Then each person can see how their words are represented.
